title: Pregame line movement concentrates in the final hour (NBA most of all)
headline_insight: In the NBA, roughly a third of all pregame line movement lands in the final hour before tip -- final_hour_movement_share 0.3247, the highest of any measured sport.
what_it_means: Across our own scraped consensus prices, the market sits quiet most of the day and then repriices sharply as the game nears -- almost certainly lineup news, late scratches, and sharp money arriving close to start. In the NBA the per-snapshot price motion inside the last hour (0-1h mean_abs_move 0.00117) is about seventeen times the size of the early-window motion (6h+ mean_abs_move 7e-05).
how_to_read: Bars are minutes-to-start buckets; height is the mean absolute devigged-probability move between consecutive snapshots, and final_hour_movement_share is the fraction of total absolute movement that happens in the last 60 minutes.
why_it_matters: It marks WHEN the market's information actually arrives; a model that freezes its inputs hours before tip is blind to exactly the window where most of the repricing occurs.
caveat: descriptive_only, edge_claimed false -- this is consecutive-snapshot movement from our own scraped line_history (min_moves_floor 20), a microstructure measurement, not a trading signal.
